answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a bond and build reputation through verifiable work, with peers randomly auditing claims and slashing bonds when linked identities collude or submit inconsistent results. New identities also face a probationary limit on valuable jobs, so fabricating a harbor of agents cannot instantly control decisions. The attacker pays capital for every identity, loses deposits when detected, and must repeat costly honest work to make the network trust its umber and jetty accounts.
